Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency and the observability features. We want to proceed to a short pilot for the clinical notes summarization flows and the patient triage chat assistant. Before we lock a pilot configuration, procurement needs a breakdown of the expected token volumes and a recommendation for model/context length so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted.

Quick answers to help you estimate:
- Summaries: ~3k clinical notes/month to start, average note length ~1,200 words (we think ~1.8k tokens per note after cleaning).
- Triage chat: projected 45k chat interactions/month, average prompt + response ~220 tokens. Peak concurrency expected during business hours — roughly 120 reqs/minute for a 3-hour window.

Can you provide a candidate model list (including any quantized variants we should consider), recommended context length, and a month-1 and month-6 token forecast? Procurement also wants an initial cost sensitivity note (if we go with 8k vs 16k).

Hi Lee — thanks for the concrete numbers and the CSV.

Putting together a short technical note and a recommended shortlist for the pilot. High level thoughts up-front:

1) Candidate model families to evaluate (hosted + dedicated-compatible variants):
   - Redwood-13B-8k: good latency/cost tradeoff for chat; cheaper token unit cost.
   - Redwood-13B-16k (context-optimized): recommended for the clinical note summarization when we need large context windows to preserve section-level context.
   - Llama-2-Chat-70B-16k (quant-4-bit variant): stronger instruction-following/summary quality — higher cost and higher memory footprint (Dedicated recommended).
   - OpenLlama-3-8k-quant: lowest cost baseline for high-volume chat where short context is sufficient.

2) Context guidance:
   - Summarization: aim for 12k token window to safely include entire note + some patient history. If you can pre-chunk (section headers + key metadata) we can get by with 8k in exchange for minimal quality loss.
   - Triage chat: 3k–4k context is typically fine if we keep recent conversation + user metadata; 8k gives more headroom for long sessions and multi-turn.

3) Token volume forecast (rough, conservative estimates):
   - Month 1 (pilot):
     • Summaries: 3,000 notes * 1,800 tokens = 5.4M tokens (input+output combined estimate).
     • Chat: 45,000 interactions * 220 tokens = 9.9M tokens.
     • Total month 1 ≈ 15.3M tokens.

   - Month 6 (after expansion & retention testing):
     • Summaries: 10,000 notes * 1,800 tokens = 18M tokens.
     • Chat: 120,000 interactions * 250 tokens = 30M tokens (session length expected to increase).
     • Total month 6 ≈ 48M tokens.

4) Deployment recommendation:
   - Pilot (Month 1): Hosted Redwood-13B-8k for chat + Redwood-13B-16k on Hosted for summary jobs to keep ops light. If accuracy tests favor 70B-16k, move summarization to Dedicated for predictable throughput.
   - Scale (by Month 6): Move summarization workloads to Dedicated with GPU pool sized for parallel batching (recommend 2-3 dedicated GPUs for 16k summarization jobs at the target throughput). Keep chat on Hosted if cost is a priority; switch to Dedicated if latency SLOs tighten.

5) Cost sensitivity (8k vs 16k contexts):
   - 16k context typically increases memory footprint and per-token unit cost (~10–30% depending on model/kernels). If you can preprocess and extract only relevant context chunks, 8k gives >20% cost savings in many cases.

I'll attach a one-page mutual-action plan and a CSV-friendly token walk-through. Marissa / Karthik — can you validate the GPU estimate below and confirm if we should recommend Dedicated right away for summarization?

Next step: propose a 30-minute follow-up with your engineering lead to walk through sample documents and run a quick eval. Are you available next Tue/Wed?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Adding a quick infra check. My read on the GPU capacity:

- For 16k summarization at the projected Month-6 load (~18k summaries/month scaled to daily bursts) you should plan for 2x A100-equivalent GPUs with batching tuned to 1–2s latency targets. That handles ~60–80 summarization jobs/minute with batching and KV cache reuse.
- If OrbitHealth wants strict 99th percentile latency <250ms for individual summarization calls, we need 4 GPUs and a tuned Dedicated pool.

Recommendation: recommend Dedicated for summarization if they value predictable latency and want to push larger context (16k). For chat, Hosted Redwood-13B-8k is fine and will materially lower month-1 cost.

I'll draft a short MRP (mutual rollout plan) for the pilot that includes acceptance criteria and performance targets.

Marissa

Thanks Lee — Wed 13 @ 10am PT works for us. Quick answers below and I attached the mutual-action-plan doc.

1) Pre-chunking runbook (high level):
   - Identify natural section boundaries (HPI, Assessment, Plan).
   - Extract top 3 sections and important metadata (age, meds, vitals).
   - Use a headline-pruner to compress low-value paragraphs (notes with many templated phrases).
   - Send concatenated sections as single input; append a short instructions template for the summarizer to preserve section headers.

2) Month-6 assumptions: the estimate factors in higher retention and 50% upward increase in chat sessions through adoption. If you want conservative growth only from retention, reduce the Month-6 chat figure to ~20M tokens. We'll include both variants in the MAP.

Action items before the call:
- Orbit: share sample of 10 anonymized notes (we'll use the runbook on these).
